title: Migrate the Intake Record to Schema v2
scenario: The desk approved a breaking change to the intake schema: v2 renames a field, splits prices into value plus unit, and stamps every record with its schema version. Three downstream consumers read this record. Your job: migrate a v1 record to v2 exactly - because 'almost migrated' breaks consumers in ways 'not migrated' never does.
input:
Existing v1 record (market-intake.json):
{ "hub": "ERCOT", "peakPrice": "$187/MWh", "settledPrice": "$142/MWh", "generationFlag": "Wind underperformed", "approvalRequired": true }

Migration spec v1 -> v2 (approved by the Desk Manager):
1. Add schemaVersion: "2.0.0" - every record must self-identify from now on.
2. Prices become plain numbers; the unit moves to a single priceUnit field: "USD/MWh".
3. generationFlag is RENAMED to operatingSignal (same value; the old name confused readers - it was never a boolean flag).
4. approvalRequired is unchanged.
5. Add migratedFrom: "1.0.0" so the record's history is traceable.
instructions: Apply all five migration rules to the v1 record - no more, no less.
Strip price formatting: the numbers become plain numbers, the unit becomes its own field.
Rename generationFlag to operatingSignal, keeping its value.
Return the migrated v2 record, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Migrate this v1 intake record to v2: add schemaVersion 2.0.0, make peakPrice and settledPrice plain numbers with the unit in a separate priceUnit field (USD/MWh), rename generationFlag to operatingSignal keeping its value, keep approvalRequired, and add migratedFrom 1.0.0.
successMessage: Record migrated to v2. Every downstream consumer can now check schemaVersion before reading - the contract is explicit.

intro.heading: Before you build: schemas are contracts, and contracts change

sections.title: Why breaking changes get versions
sections.body: Risk Evaluation, Approval Decision, and the Morning Brief all read this record. Rename a field silently and they break silently. Stamp schemaVersion on every record and consumers can check the contract before trusting the contents - the difference between an upgrade and an outage.

sections.title: A migration is a mapping, not a rewrite
sections.body: Every v2 field traces to a v1 field or to the spec: renamed (generationFlag to operatingSignal), reshaped (price strings to number plus unit), added (schemaVersion, migratedFrom), or carried (approvalRequired, hub). If you cannot name a field's origin, you are inventing data.

sections.title: Why the rename happened
sections.body: generationFlag was never a boolean - the name lied about the type. Renaming to operatingSignal is the kind of small honesty that prevents the next engineer's wrong assumption. Naming debt is real debt.

sections.title: migratedFrom is the paper trail
sections.body: A record that says migratedFrom 1.0.0 can be audited against its origin. When migrations go wrong at scale, this field is how you find which records to fix.

fieldGuide.hint: Not every field changes in a migration.

fieldGuide.meaning: The version this record came from.

takeaway.heading: Schema migrated without breakage
points: You executed a breaking change as a disciplined mapping: rename, reshape, add, carry - every v2 field traceable to its origin.
schemaVersion turns an implicit contract into a checkable one; consumers can refuse records they do not understand.
migratedFrom preserves lineage, which is what makes bad migrations findable and fixable at scale.
This is the change-management pattern behind every API version bump and every database migration you will ever run.
The workflow can now evolve its core record's contract without breaking the consumers that trust it.
